key_insight: A structured-judgment model and several general-purpose LLMs all extracted smoking history well enough for lung cancer screening decisions, with the biggest tradeoff being latency, cost, and performance on complex cases.
clinical_relevance: For lung cancer screening CDS, fast and accurate extraction of smoking status, pack-years, and quit date from notes could support more consistent eligibility assessment in routine care.
method: 3,000 synthetic outpatient notes were created across template, realistic messy, and arithmetic-heavy messy conditions.
Compared a low-cost structured-judgment model (TypeSafe Jev 1.13) against four LLMs using the same structured output schema.
Eligibility for USPSTF 2021 and ACS 2023 screening was computed from model outputs in code.
evidence_signal: Across 3,000 notes, all systems showed high eligibility accuracy; the structured model was fastest and lowest cost, while the newest cost-efficient LLM was strongest on the most complex notes.
watch_item: Synthetic benchmark results may not fully reflect real-world note variability, and complex arithmetic cases still caused more false screening flags for the structured model.
paper_title: Extracting smoking history from clinical notes for lung cancer screening decision support: comparing a structured-judgment model with general-purpose large language models
